items.author: PBS Space Time
items.content:
<article>Book a free consultation with an Odoo expert or start a 15-day free trial of Odoo: https://www.odoo.com/r/cAT

Can adding every positive whole number really give you -1/12? We explore how physicists extract meaningful finite values from infinite sums, and how this strange mathematical technique shows up in the measurable Casimir effect and even helps explain why bosonic string theory requires 26 dimensions.

items.title: The Shocking Truth About Triton's Core
items.author: Astrum
items.content:
<article>What we found on Neptune’s moon Triton. 
Use the code "Astrum" and this link 👉 https://incogni.com/astrum to get 60% off the Annual Incogni plan!

▀▀▀▀▀▀

Triton is no ordinary moon. With an impossibly young surface and active cryovolcanoes, Neptune’s giant moon has baffled scientists for decades. How can this frozen world be so active, so far from the Sun? In this video, we’re digging into the latest discoveries, including a surprising mystery hiding deep beneath its icy crust.

items.title: What Is It Like on the Surface of a Black Hole Planet?
items.author: Astrum
items.content:
<article>Scientists are searching for missing planets in the most unlikely place. 
Astrum books are still available in the US! If you’re fascinated by the cosmos, want to learn more about our Solar System, or just love stunning space images, get your hands on an Astrum book here: https://astrumspace.co/ 

▀▀▀▀▀▀

At the edge of a supermassive black hole lies one of the most violent, hostile environments in the cosmos. It's the last place anyone expected to find a planet, but scientists now believe missing worlds could be lurking here. How do these black hole planets form? What are their surfaces like? And how do we actually find them?

items.title: The Universe May Have Just Revealed the True Nature of Empty Space
items.author: PBS Space Time
items.content:
<article>Displate’s offering up to up to for 33% off at: https://displate.com/l/spacetime when you use the code: SPACETIME

Nothing is complicated. By which I mean, everything is complicated, because in physics even completely empty space is described as being full of quantum fields doing complicated things even when nothing else is there. So if empty space has these exotic properties, what sort of crazy stuff can we make it do? One prediction that’s been around for a while is that under extreme conditions, empty space can be sort of crystalized. And there’s good evidence that we’ve observed this for the first time.

items.content:
<article>Visit https://brilliant.org/coldfusion to try Brilliant’s tutor for free and get 20% off an annual subscription.

With the release of the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18, people forget that one of the core elements of the software came in the form of a little phone called the Palm Pre in 2009. The story of the device is a wild ride and it's impact is still with us today. In this episode we explore.
